newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul officials deny planning market-boost steps.
newsitem.headline: Seoul officials deny planning market-boost steps.

text.p: South Korean finance ministry officials denied on Tuesday local media reports that the ministry was planning a package of steps to boost the sagging stock market.
"We have no such plan," an official at the ministry's securities policy department told Reuters by telephone.
The domestic Yonhap news agency quoted an unidentified senior finance ministry official as saying the steps would include banning financial firms from offering rights issues.
The report said banning rights issues by financial firms was aimed at easing fears that a huge supply of new stocks would dampen the already languishing market.
The Seoul bourse has been in the doldrums mainly due to such fears and an overhang of margin loans from brokerage houses.
Brokers estimated about 238.5 billion won worth of rights issues are scheduled for November.
Loans for margin trading valued at between 500 billion and 900 billion won must also be repaid this month.
